summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of chronic pancreatitis, type 2 diabetes, bipolar disorder, PTSD, and multiple abdominal surgeries was admitted for acute exacerbation of chronic abdominal pain following consumption of a deviled egg. He presented with severe mid-abdominal pain radiating to the left, consistent with prior pancreatitis flares. Initial concern for internal hernia was ruled out by surgery based on CT findings. The patient was managed conservatively with NPO status for two days, IV fluids, IV pain control with Dilaudid, and anti-nausea medication. He gradually advanced to a regular low-fat diet and transitioned to oral pain medications. His pain improved to baseline, and he remained stable without complications. He was discharged home with updated pain and enzyme medications, instructions for low-fat diet, and follow-up with primary care.
